title: Reference Manual on Scientific Evidence, Fourth Edition, Volume I, Guide to Economic Damages
publisher: Federal Judicial Center / National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
source_classification: judicial reference manual / nonbinding expert guide
questions: fraud loss, damages, asset dissipation, lost profits and valuation date
inspected_summary: The Guide to Economic Damages frames quantification as the difference between actual outcome and a factually supported but-for scenario, with the measure and valuation date depending on claim theory and law. title: United States Code, Title 11, §§ 501-502 and 506, Creditors and Claims
publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. House of Representatives; U.S. Government Publishing Office / GovInfo
publication_date_or_edition: 2024 edition of Title 11 U.S. Code; official GovInfo PDF retrieved September 23, 2026
accounting_bases: Bankruptcy Code claims allowance and secured-claim valuation
source_classification: federal statute, codified U.S. Code text
questions: How should debtor schedules and creditor claims be reconciled?
When is a claim allowed and what portion is secured?
inspected_summary: Section 502(a) deems a claim filed under §501 allowed unless a party in interest objects. On objection, after notice and hearing the court determines the claim amount as of the petition date and applies statutory allowance/disallowance grounds. Section 506(a)(1) makes an allowed lien-secured claim secured to the extent of the creditor’s value in estate property (or amount subject to setoff), with unsecured balance for any deficiency; valuation depends on its purpose, proposed use/disposition and related hearing. This states general federal statutory rules, not a determination of a particular claim, lien, priority or valuation.
locators: Title 11 §§501-502, PDF printed pp. 103-106; §502(a)-(b), pp.104-105; §§506(a)-(d), printed pp.116-117; source refs turn311view0 lines147-170 and turn311view1 lines1576-1626
access_limits: Directly read official GovInfo 2024 Title 11 codification. This is a general statutory read, not later-enactment verification or case-specific legal advice. Check amendments after the 2024 edition, governing rules, orders and case facts.
